The mesochile is the middle part of an orchid lip, between the hypochile and the epichile.
Mesochilium is a variant name for the mesochile.
Seed wing means the wing of a seed.
'Wing of seed' is the same as 'seed wing'.
'Aile de la graine' is the French for 'seed wing'.
A bare 'burl' is often a woody swelling on a trunk or branch, not a lignotuber. It is only a lignotuber when it sits at the base or root crown.
A root crown burl is a basal woody swelling, which is a lignotuber.
A basal burl is a lignotuber.
Calyx limb is the expanded upper part of a fused calyx.
Plural of 'calyx limb'.
'Limbe du calice' is the French for 'calyx limb'.
'Limbe calicinal' is the French for 'calyx limb'.
A lobe of the floral disc. In Asteraceae 'disc' means disc florets, so this could be misread there, but that is unlikely with this wording.
Plural of 'disc lobe'. The same Asteraceae caveat applies.
'Disk' is a spelling variant of 'disc'.
'Lobe du disque' is the French for 'disc lobe'.
'Vagrant' is not a botanical term. It is probably an OCR or spelling error for 'vaginant'. Fix it as a spelling correction only after checking the source text; do not map it as a synonym.
Same as R3518: 'vagrant laminae' is not a botanical term and is probably an error for 'vaginant laminae'.
A tooth is a shallower division than a lobe, so mapping 'tooth' to 'lobe' loses the difference. Keep this for lobes only, or use a separate tooth class.
'Involucral tooth' is a tooth, not a lobe. See R3520.
Involucral lobes are lobes of the involucre.
'Phalange' is the French and old botanical word for a stamen bundle, as in Hypericum.
A stamen bundle is a stamen fascicle.
A staminal fascicle is a stamen fascicle.
A staminal phalange is a stamen bundle.
A staminal bundle is a stamen fascicle.
A stamen phalanx is a stamen bundle.
In floras 'phalanx' means a stamen bundle. Check any context outside flowers.
Plural of 'phalanx'. Same caveat as R3529.
Guide cells are the deuter cells next to the vascular bundles in leaf anatomy of Cyperaceae and mosses.
Deuter cells are the guide cells.
'Deuters' is short for 'deuter cells'.
A stomatal line is a line of stomata.
Plural of 'stomatal line'.
A stomatal row is a line of stomata.
'Line of stomata' is the same as 'stomatal line'.
Laminal cells are cells of the leaf lamina, mainly in moss descriptions.
'Lamina cells' is the same as 'laminal cells'.

'Leaf cells' covers every cell of the leaf, including costa, alar and marginal cells, not only the lamina. It should map to a general leaf cell class, or be mapped only when the text is clearly about the lamina.
'Male zone' is a spadix zone only in Araceae and similar plants. Apply it only when the container is a spadix.
'Staminate zone' can refer to other inflorescences, so require a spadix container.
The text names the spadix, so the male portion of the spadix is its staminate zone.
The spadix staminate part is the staminate zone.
The staminate part of the spadix is the staminate zone.
The male zone of the spadix is the staminate zone.
The male part of the spadix is the staminate zone.
'Zone mâle' is a spadix zone only in Araceae. Require a spadix container.
A rostellum lobe is a lobe of the orchid rostellum.
'Rostellar lobe' is the adjective form of 'rostellum lobe'.
